copilot-app-builder.title: FAQ: App Builder in Microsoft 365 Copilot – Microsoft Learn
copilot-app-builder.notes: App Builder is an agent inside Microsoft Copilot that lets people describe an app in everyday language and have it generated, saved and shared. The resulting apps are meant for interactive prototypes, data visualization and productivity tools for the author or their team. The AI produces code from the description and builds app pages in real time during a conversational exchange, and users can keep refining elements, layout and behavior afterwards. Context such as images, people, tags, meetings and Word, PowerPoint or Excel documents can be supplied as input, and users can rate results with thumbs up or down and comments. Documented limits: complex design requirements are difficult, data connections are restricted to Microsoft Lists with create, read, update and delete operations, the generated code cannot be edited by hand, and only English is supported. The page advises describing simple problems clearly and testing apps thoroughly before sharing them. It also notes that app building is now offered in Copilot Cowork and is planned for Microsoft Copilot Studio.

copilot-flex-routing.title: Copilot flex routing – Microsoft Learn
copilot-flex-routing.notes: Flex routing is a setting for customers in the EU and EFTA that lets large language model inferencing take place outside the EU Data Boundary during periods of high demand, so Copilot stays consistent under load. It applies to Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Chat in the Microsoft 365 admin center, and to Copilot experiences in Dynamics 365, Power Platform and Copilot Studio in the Power Platform admin center. When active, processing may occur in the United States, Canada or Australia, while data stays encrypted in transit and at rest, and stored data remains inside the EU Data Boundary apart from limited pseudonymized data kept for security and operations. An administrator with the AI Administrator role chooses between allowing flex routing during peak load or not allowing it, and can change the choice at any time. The Power Platform setting inherits the Microsoft 365 choice unless it is stricter. Tenants using Multi-Geo are out of scope for the Microsoft 365 setting. For eligible tenants created after late March 2026 it is on by default, and older tenants are asked to review it.

copilot-researcher-agent.title: Researcher agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot – Microsoft Learn
copilot-researcher-agent.notes: Researcher is an assistant within Microsoft Copilot built for complex, multi-step research tasks and produces well-sourced, comprehensive reports. It draws on web information as well as work content the user can already access, such as files, emails, meetings and chats, and it respects the same permissions, policies and compliance rules as the rest of the work environment. Output can include structured sections, charts and other visualizations, and citations. The agent may ask clarifying questions so the person can steer the work, and the search scope can be set to work resources, the web, or both. It is reached by signing in to the Microsoft Copilot app and choosing it under Agents in chat. Typical uses are analyses combining several sources and reports meant for sharing or decisions. Because processing takes longer, it is less suitable for quick tasks such as summarizing a short email, where standard Copilot Chat is recommended. Result quality depends on precise prompts and a clearly defined search scope.

copilot-studio-topics.title: Create and edit topics – Microsoft Copilot Studio
copilot-studio-topics.notes: A topic in Copilot Studio defines one part of the conversation between a user and an agent. It is built on an authoring canvas from one or more nodes, each performing an action such as sending a message or asking a question, which together set the possible conversation paths. This gives a no-code way for an agent to answer questions, take actions and resolve problems. System topics cover basics like escalating to a person or ending a conversation; they cannot be created or deleted but can be turned off and edited. Custom topics include predefined ones such as greeting and any the maker creates. Node types include message, question, adaptive card, condition, variable management, topic management, tools and advanced nodes for generative answers or HTTP requests. Trigger phrases should be short, and with classic orchestration the agent matches topics by phrases and language understanding, while generative orchestration chooses topics from their descriptions. A code editor with YAML is available, though designing complex topics fully in code is not fully supported. Topic names should avoid periods, because such an agent cannot be exported as a solution.

credit-and-collections.title: Credit and collections overview – Dynamics 365 Finance – Microsoft Learn
credit-and-collections.notes: This overview covers two related areas of accounts receivable in Dynamics 365 Finance. Credit management controls customer credit limits and uses rule-based credit rules to decide how sales orders move through posting. Collections management handles receivables and the collection activities needed when payments are overdue. On the credit side, users maintain credit attributes for assessing customers, create limits including temporary adjustments, record insurance and guarantees, and group customers so they share one limit. Risk scores can be assigned and used to generate limits automatically. Blocking rules place orders on hold based on factors such as risk, payment terms, limit, overdue amounts and limit utilization, and a workflow can approve limit changes and order releases. On the collections side, a central Collections page offers customer lists built from predefined criteria and customer pools, including pools per collector, with all collection information for a customer on one page. Interest and fees can be waived, reinstated or reversed, write-offs created and non-sufficient-funds payments processed in a single step, and customer aging snapshots capture aging as of a date. The page is a conceptual overview and points to separate setup articles.

custom-pages.title: Custom pages overview for model-driven apps – Power Apps – Microsoft Learn
custom-pages.notes: A custom page is a page type for model-driven apps that brings canvas app capabilities into them. It can appear as a full page, a dialog or a side panel, and it is authored in Power Apps Studio with low-code formulas and custom Power Apps component framework controls. Compared with forms, views and dashboards it is more flexible: it can bind to one or more tables, works with Dataverse and the Power Apps connectors, and supports responsive layouts through responsive container controls. Navigation uses the Power Fx navigate function, and model-driven pages open a custom page through the navigateTo client API; pages can also be added to the site map. It must be created from within a solution, is a single solution component that only one maker can edit at a time, and follows the licensing and sharing of the model-driven app. A model-driven app can contain up to 25 custom pages. Standalone canvas apps are not supported as custom pages, and embedded canvas apps remain limited to forms. The page positions custom pages as the usual replacement for embedded canvas apps.

customer-intent-agent.title: Set up the Customer Intent Agent – Dynamics 365 Contact Center – Microsoft Learn
customer-intent-agent.notes: The Customer Intent Agent discovers customer intents from historical data and maintains a current intent library whose entries carry attributes for intent detection, interviewing and fulfillment. The stated aim is higher deflection rates, and intent plus interview answers also improve generated responses for Copilot agents and human service representatives. On escalation, the intent and the interview questions already asked are passed along so the representative can address open items. Each intent is switched on for use through a checkbox labelled Use in AI Agents, and a component collection called intent-based suggestions is added in Microsoft Copilot Studio with topics for the main flow and a plugin. Redirect variables control hand-offs for resolved issues, unknown intent, inability to proceed, customer-requested escalation and errors, while an enrichment context variable carries data collected earlier, for example from a pre-chat survey. Requirements include enabled intent discovery, a Copilot agent linked to a knowledge source and an omnichannel workstream, the Environment Maker role, and a Dataverse connection reference configured by an administrator. By default users must be authenticated to Dataverse for the library, and component updates only arrive after the agent is republished manually.
